verdict.reasoning: Patient reports waking with a painful left-sided headache at about 5:30: "woke up this morning... really horrible pain on the left side of my head" and "probably around, five thirty ish."

Severity/new intensity supported by: "nothing as severe as this before." Mild photophobia supported by: "I'm a little bit sensitive [to bright lights] it just, it kind of, makes my eyes a little bit sore, but nothing that I can't really handle."
Patient states: "When I first got up this morning, my head felt a bit dizzy, but that's kind of subsided now." This supports brief morning dizziness.

Patient describes initial worsening then improvement when lying down: "when I lay down... it kind of feels a little bit sore at first... so yeah, at the beginning it does, but then again that's just kind of, um, soothes a little bit" and agrees it's ultimately better lying down.
Paracetamol was ineffective: "I've taken some Paracetamol." and when asked if it helped: "Um, not really, no."

No fever/neck stiffness explicitly denied: "do you have any neck stiffness at all?" "Uh, no." and "do you have any fever?" "No." No nausea supported by: "are you feeling nauseous at all?" "Um, not really... my head felt a bit dizzy... that's kind of subsided now." Vomiting is not mentioned; stating its absence is a reasonable implicit negative in this context.

History of milder frontal headaches: patient says prior headaches "tends to be, a bit of a cluster at the front of my head" and "I've, had a bit of a history with headaches, but nothing as severe as this before."

Transcript confirms anxiety and duration but not a formal GAD diagnosis: "I've had, um, so I had, like anxiety for about, two years now, and I've been on, uh, Sertraline for, a while." It does not specify "Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD)."
Patient confirms current Sertraline use: "I've been on, uh, Sertraline for, a while." and when asked if taking it now: "Yes."
Current-day Paracetamol use: "in terms of um, this, headache since this morning, have you taken anything for it yet?" "Um, I've taken some Paracetamol."
Patient denies medication allergies: "Do you have any allergies to any medication?" "Not that I'm aware of, no."
Family history: "are there any illnesses in your family?" Patient: "my mum's had a history of anxiety as well but, no kind of like physical illnesses or anything like that."
No family migraine/major illness: "does anyone in your family have any migraines... ?" "Uh, no. They haven't." and later: "no kind of like physical illnesses or anything like that."

Work stress and late nights for ~2 months: "work's kind of, um, a bit stressful... I've got a lot going on" and "I've kind of, been, doing a lot of late nights as well"; duration: "for probably about a couple of months now."
Exercise: "normally I, try to go running at least three times a week."
Living situation: "are you living by yourself... or with someone else?" Patient: "Um, I live with my partner."
Smoking status: "Are you a smoker?" Patient: "No."
Pets: "do you have any pets at home?" Patient: "Uh, I have a cat."

Acute unilateral headache supported by history. Doctor’s assessment: "it sounds like it might be one of two things. It could be an element of what we call tension headache... The other possibility is, um, migraine as well."

Work-related stress and anxiety on Sertraline are documented (see sh-001 and med-001). Current stability: patient says anxiety is limited and manageable: "sometimes I do feel a bit anxious... but other than that, I, I don't, feel, um, massively anxious."

Plan: "the things that we'd start off first line, if someone had migraine... would be to start Ibuprofen... You can keep on taking Paracetamol as well if you like, but the, the Ibuprofen's um, actually more effective."
Hydration advice: "you're drinking a minimum of, um, one point five to two litres uh, of water or fluids a day, and that's not including coffee or tea."
Sleep advice: "ensure that you're having a minimum of seven, eight hours sleep at night, every night."
Sick leave suggestion: "maybe consider taking some time off work... maybe having a week off if you self-certify, that might help with things."
Counseling referral: "I'd also like you to explore, counselling options as well so there's, a counselling service in your area, that I can give you the link for, for you to self-refer."

Written red-flag info and safety netting: "there'll be a summary of all of this in the notes. Um, and I'll also leave a link, to some of the danger signs of symptoms of headaches, in the notes... what kind of things, should trigger you contacting another doctor." Also: "if anything changes in the meantime, or you get worried or things get worse... we can reassess the situation."

Follow-up in 1 week: "we'll have a follow-up in a week's time" and later "we'll touch base in a week's time, with me or, myself or one of the other doctors." The initial and follow-up are via the same remote consultation service (video/phone); specifying "video" is an acceptable inference.
